title: Will AI-powered autonomous weapons obey the laws of war?
key_facts: AI is increasingly part of modern conflicts, helping militaries analyse intelligence, identify targets and support battlefield operations.
Supporters say AI could make warfare more precise and protect civilians; critics say some decisions should never be delegated to machines.
DW asks whether laws written after World War II can still regulate warfare in the age of AI.
Guests are Bonnie Docherty of Harvard Law School and Human Rights Watch, and Laurie R. Blank of Emory University School of Law.
quote_evidence: Artificial intelligence is rapidly becoming part of modern conflicts.
